say: This measures how much a plant grows from one photo to the next. No neural network and no paid API — just a green-hue threshold in HSV colour space, counting how many pixels are leaf.
Three frames of the same plant, framed the same way each time. It is an illustration, so you can see plainly what gets counted — the measurement underneath is the real thing.

One plant per photo, taken from a fixed spot, so I switch off multi-plant detection. That measures leaf area against the whole frame — which is exactly what a fixed-camera time series wants, and it avoids a trap where cropping to each plant hides the growth.

The chart reads leaf area against the first photo: up about 170 percent by the second frame, and over 400 percent by the third. The plant genuinely has far more green in it, and the count reflects that.
And here is the check that it measured the plant and not the room: the magenta overlay on each thumbnail is exactly the pixels counted as leaf. The pot and the wall are left out.

One caveat the tool states plainly: these percentages are relative leaf area, not a real-world size in centimetres, and they only hold up if every photo is framed the same way. Consistent framing matters here far more than a fancy camera.
